subject: economics
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 have two parts of 1 mark each.
Section C: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words. Show the working in numerical questions.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: Give one word: (a) Goods used only once, e.g. milk or coal. (b) Goods used again and again, e.g. a scooter or a machine.
State True or False: (a) Roads constructed by the government are production. (b) Purchase of a tractor by a farmer is consumption.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) False — a tractor adds to the farmer's capital stock, so it is investment (capital formation) for production, not consumption.

questions.q: State True or False: (a) In a foreign production unit, foreigners contribute more than 50% of the capital. (b) A production unit owned by two or more persons is a partnership.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) True — a partnership has 2 to 20 owners.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Rent is a ______ cost. (b) Wages are a ______ cost.
State True or False: (a) AR and MR are equal when every unit sells at the same price. (b) Implicit costs have bills and receipts.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) False — implicit costs are self-supplied, so no money is paid; explicit costs have bills.

questions.q: Give one word: (a) Car and petrol are ______ goods. (b) The definition of demand includes price, quantity and ______.
Give one word: (a) The definition of supply includes price, time and ______. (b) The quantity with a seller at a point of time.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The currency of the USA is the ______. (b) The common currency of Europe is the ______.
Complete: A bank receives a deposit of ₹200 and lends ₹180. (a) Primary deposit = ? (b) Total deposit after the loan = ?
Fill in the blanks: (a) Unpublished secondary data include internal reports of ______. (b) They also include research reports of ______.
State True or False: (a) There are not various measures of central tendency. (b) The arithmetic mean is a measure of central tendency.
questions.answer:
(a) False — there are several (mean, median, mode).
(b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The ______ sector pays more than the agricultural sector. (b) Agriculture belongs to the ______ sector.
Match: (a) Selling to foreign citizens — ? (b) International trade leads to — ? [specialisation / exports]
Give one word: (a) A resource that gets replenished over time. (b) Reusing rainwater collected from roofs.
State True or False: (a) A consumer buys both goods and services. (b) The CPA covers only the private sector.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) False — it covers the private, public and cooperative sectors.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the free services used in daily consumption with an example.
questions.answer:
Free services cannot be bought in the market. They are given out of love and affection.
Example: parents caring for their children, or a mother cooking dinner for the family.

questions.q: Explain consumption as a basic economic activity.
questions.answer:
Consumption is the use of goods and services for the direct satisfaction of individual or collective wants, such as a household buying food, clothes, a cycle or a doctor's service.
It is the goal of production.

questions.q: Three firms A, B and C supply 10, 15 and 20 kg of a commodity at ₹100. Find the market supply.
questions.answer: Market supply = sum of individual supplies = 10 + 15 + 20 = 45 kg at ₹100.

questions.q: What is the barter system? Give an example.
questions.answer: Barter is the exchange of goods and services for other goods and services without money. Examples: 10 kg of wheat for 5 kg of sugar, or 8 kg of rice for a pair of shoes.

questions.q: What credit do development banks provide?
questions.answer: Development banks give long-term credit to private companies and public sector units to set up industries and build infrastructure, e.g. IDBI, IFCI and State Finance Corporations.

or.q: Distinguish between a lender and a borrower.
or.answer: The lender gives money as a loan and has the right to claim it back with interest, e.g. a bank. The borrower takes the loan now and promises to repay it later with interest.

questions.q: 'Statistics are numerically expressed.' Explain.
questions.answer: Only facts put into numbers by counting, measuring or estimating are statistics, e.g. 409 students admitted to a college. Qualities such as good or ugly cannot be quantified, so they are not statistics.

questions.q: Explain the concept of central tendency.
questions.answer: Central tendency is the tendency of data to cluster around a central value. The average (e.g. the arithmetic mean) measures it and gives one representative value for the whole data.

questions.q: How do rural people earn a living?
questions.answer: Through agriculture and allied activities (crops, livestock, poultry, dairy), forestry (timber, firewood, herbs), fishery and mining.

or.answer: Timber, firewood, herbal medicines, bamboo and grass (for paper).

questions.q: Distinguish between imports and exports.
questions.answer:
Exports: selling domestic goods and services to citizens of foreign countries, which earns foreign exchange.
Imports: buying goods and services from foreign countries, which uses foreign exchange.

questions.q: Name two kinds of environmental degradation.
questions.answer:
(1) Soil degradation — loss of soil quality and fertility.
(2) Habitat degradation — loss of a habitat's ability to support native life.

questions.q: Explain the right to information.
questions.answer: Sellers must give full information — price, weight, brand, manufacturing and expiry dates, ingredients, quality marks and contact details — so consumers can make informed choices. Example: an air fare of ₹1,500 turned out to be ₹4,995 with hidden taxes.

or.q: Explain the right to consumer education.
or.answer: Consumers have the right to programmes and information that help them decide before and after purchase — government and NGO guidelines and awareness of marks such as ISI, AGMARK and BIS.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What are the functions of an entrepreneur?
questions.answer:
(1) Brings land, labour and capital together in the right proportion.
(2) Decides what and how much to produce and how much to spend on factors.
(3) Bears the risk and uncertainty of production.
(4) Pays rent, wages and interest, arranges the sale of output and earns profit.

questions.q: How do climatic conditions affect market demand?
questions.answer:
Market demand changes with the season.
In summer, demand rises for ice, cold drinks, coolers and cotton clothes.
In the rainy season, demand rises for umbrellas and raincoats.
In winter, demand rises for woollens and heaters.
So the same good is in high demand in one season and low demand in another.

questions.q: An urban unemployed person wants a loan to start a small business. Which bank should they approach and why?
questions.answer:
They should approach an urban cooperative bank (or a commercial bank).
Urban cooperative banks give credit for self-employment activities, small-scale industry and personal finance at reasonable terms.
Commercial banks also give loans to start businesses to people able to repay in future.

questions.q: What is central tendency? State two precautions in using the arithmetic mean.
questions.answer:
Central tendency is the tendency of data to cluster around a central value, measured by an average.
Precautions: (1) The mean is a theoretical value that may not exist in fact — 2.7 children per family is impossible for any one family. (2) The mean cannot be used for qualitative data such as honesty or beauty.

questions.q: 'The primary sector provides raw materials to industries.' Explain.
questions.answer:
Many industries depend on agriculture.
Sugar mills need sugarcane, jute mills need jute, textile mills need cotton, and vanaspati needs oilseeds.
Paper needs grass and bamboo.
The food-processing industry (pickles, jam, juice, biscuits) runs on farm produce.

questions.q: 'Habitat degradation reduces the carrying capacity of an area.' Explain.
questions.answer:
Carrying capacity is the number of plants and animals of a species an area can support.
When forests are cut and land is cleared, food and shelter are lost, so fewer animals and plants can survive there.
Populations fall, food chains are upset, and species may become extinct.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: State and explain the law of diminishing marginal product of labour.
questions.answer:
Law: when more units of a variable factor (labour) are added to fixed factors, MP first rises, then falls, and may become negative.
Reason: at first the extra workers share work efficiently, so MP rises. Beyond a point the fixed machine is over-used and extra workers add less and less.
Example: MP 10, 12, 14, then 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, −2. TP is at its maximum (56) when MP = 0, so labour should not be increased beyond that point.

questions.q: Explain the consumer redressal system in India.
questions.answer:
Laws: the Consumer Protection Act 1986 is the most important law, giving cheap, simple and quick justice for all goods and services. Others are PFA 1954, ECA 1955 and SWMA 1976.
Councils: the Central Consumer Protection Council (headed by the Union minister) and State Councils.
Consumer courts (quasi-judicial, three tiers): District Consumer Forums (604, up to ₹20 lakh), State Commissions (35, up to ₹1 crore), and the National Commission (above ₹1 crore). Relief should come within 90–150 days, with appeals to the higher tier.
NGOs also help consumers file cases.
